relationship: Moving an object relative to a converging lens changes where principal rays meet and therefore image position, size and orientation; moving a screen tests whether that image can be projected.

learnerLoop.action: Predict the image, move the object, and move the screen to test the ray construction.
learnerLoop.modelChange: Object distance determines real, virtual or focal-limit image geometry; screen distance changes ray separation at the screen.
learnerLoop.evidence: Principal rays, image markings and the screen projection show image type and whether the screen is sharply focused.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Explain the result and compare object positions beyond, at and inside the focal landmarks.

invariants: The ray construction, image position, magnification and orientation agree with the same thin-lens geometry.
A virtual image is shown by backward extensions and cannot be brought to focus on the real screen.
The focal-limit case remains distinct from a finite real or virtual image.
safeAdaptations: Adjust prompts, pacing and object examples while retaining object and screen manipulation.
Add comparison positions within the supported thin-lens model.
nonGoals: Do not replace the ray investigation with calculation-only exercises.
Do not imply that aberrations or thick-lens effects are simulated.

goal.visibility: Present in the current investigation; child controls follow the mode and state.

bench.description: Object, lens, rays, focal landmarks and screen on one optical axis.
bench.visibility: Present in the current investigation; child controls follow the mode and state.

task.description: Prediction, physical test and result replace one another beside the bench.
task.visibility: Present in the current investigation; child controls follow the mode and state.

evidence.description: Projection sharpness, image geometry and persistent observation record.
evidence.visibility: Present in the current investigation; child controls follow the mode and state.

completion.description: Recorded image evidence and next investigation or practice.
completion.visibility: Visible after the required object position and screen test.

object-distance.description: Distance u from the fixed lens.
object-distance.source: Target given; learner moves the object.
object-distance.output: Determines real, focal-limit or virtual image geometry.

screen-distance.description: Distance of the physical screen from the lens.
screen-distance.source: Learner moves the screen after positioning the object.
screen-distance.output: Ray separation and projected image test whether light meets there.

image.description: Image distance, magnification, orientation and projectability.
image.domain: Thin-lens geometry, including parallel rays at F.
image.source: Computed from the same object distance and fixed focal length.
image.output: Rays, image marker, live values and projection agree.

modes.guided: Four successive object regions, each with prediction and physical test.
modes.practice: Generated image-region, relationship and mixed examples after guided work.
modes.free: Preset or direct object/screen changes; return to generated practice. No Working visibility toggle.

dependencies: Prediction unlocks object movement; matching the target unlocks screen testing.
Real images require focus; at F requires screen samples at 12 and 32 cm; virtual case tests the screen at 8 cm.
implementation.completion: completePhase records the current ray evidence after maybeMatchObject and maybeMatchScreen satisfy that case.
limitations: Thin-lens model; does not model aberrations or thick lenses.
